result.rationale: The diff shows SalesforceCalendarService's constructor (the connection init path) now unconditionally fetches a fresh token from login.salesforce.com and updates the credential in the DB on every instantiation, throwing HttpError on `response.statusText !== "OK"` — an unreliable check versus response.ok, and it hard-fails Salesforce usage on transient errors even with valid stored tokens. It also bypasses refreshOAuthTokens/parseRefreshTokenResponse's shared flow inconsistently (it uses parseRefreshTokenResponse but not refreshOAuthTokens, so sharing mode requires local SF keys). All mechanism

judged_text: Salesforce now eagerly refreshes tokens and writes to the DB in the constructor path on every service instantiation (every booking/check), hammering the SF token endpoint and hard-failing all Salesforce usage on any transient SF error even when the stored token is valid; the response.statusText !== 'OK' check is unreliable (should be response.ok) since proxies/HTTP2 can strip the reason phrase causing a spurious 400 on HTTP 200, and Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely so sharing mode still requires locally configured SF app keys
